bill.title: Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act

industries.rationale: Life insurers and annuity providers rely on death records to process claims and prevent fraudulent payments to deceased beneficiaries.
Banks and financial institutions use death records to manage accounts, prevent fraud, and comply with payment verification requirements.

bill.plainSummary: This bill makes permanent the Treasury Department's access to Social Security death records to prevent payments from being sent to deceased individuals. It requires the Social Security Administration to have clear and convincing evidence before marking someone as deceased in its master file. If someone is incorrectly listed as dead, the SSA can notify federal and state agencies that provide benefits so the error can be corrected.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

industries.rationale: The prior authorization model directly affects hospitals and physician groups by requiring advance approval for certain Medicare services they provide.
Third-party contractors processing prior authorization requests are typically health insurers or related entities that would lose revenue from this model's termination.
The model specifically requires enhanced technology and artificial intelligence systems for processing authorization requests, affecting technology vendors serving the healthcare sector.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Medicare pilot program that began in January 2026 in six states. The program requires third-party contractors to use enhanced technology, including artificial intelligence, to review and approve certain Medicare services before they are provided. The contractors are paid based on a share of any savings generated. This resolution would stop the program from continuing.

bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone whose personal data is held by a company.

The subject terms indicate it may involve competition rules, administrative enforcement, and oversight of drug pricing.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects the 10% tariff on Canadian energy and energy resources.
The 25% tariff on most Canadian imports affects manufacturers who source materials, components, or finished goods from Canada.
Retailers importing consumer goods from Canada face the 25% tariff that this resolution would eliminate.
Agricultural products and food imports from Canada are subject to the 25% tariff.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on February 1, 2025, which imposed a 25% tariff on most goods imported from Canada and a 10% tariff on Canadian energy imports. Terminating the emergency would remove the legal basis for these additional duties on Canadian products.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys imported goods, and people who make goods here.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Brazil.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: Manufacturers importing Brazilian goods or components would see tariff costs change if the emergency and its 40% duty are terminated.
Retailers and consumer-goods companies importing products from Brazil would face different import costs depending on whether the tariff remains.
Agricultural importers bringing in Brazilian food products would be affected by the removal or continuation of the 40% tariff.
Importers of Brazilian metals and minerals face tariff exposure, though precious metals were already exempted from the additional duty.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on July 30, 2025, which allowed the imposition of an additional 40% tariff on most goods imported from Brazil. Ending the emergency would remove the legal basis for those extra tariffs. Certain products—including aircraft parts, wood pulp, precious metals, energy products, and fertilizers—were already exempt from the additional tariff.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys imported goods, and people who make goods here.

bill.title: Shenandoah Mountain Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 214.
subjects: Wilderness and natural areas, wildlife refuges, wild rivers, habitats

industries.rationale: Wilderness and scenic-area designations typically restrict or prohibit mineral extraction and energy development on the designated lands.
Wilderness designations generally prohibit new mining claims and mineral extraction activities on the affected acreage.
Creation of a national scenic area and wilderness areas may affect tourism, recreation services, and visitor access in the region.
Wilderness designations can affect grazing permits and other agricultural uses of federal forest land, though the bill does not specify existing uses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create a new national scenic area covering approximately 92,562 acres of federal forest land in Virginia within the George Washington and Jefferson National Forest. It would also designate four separate wilderness areas totaling about 26,896 acres within that forest, adding them to the National Wilderness Preservation System. These designations would impose stricter land-use and conservation rules on the affected acreage.

plain.whoItTouches: People who visit public land, and people who live beside it. People who live near or work on federal land.
